source_text: Ta is discipulus spiritalis vere recipiens Spiritum Dei, qui ab initio in universis dispositionibus Dei adfuit hominibus, et futura annuntiavit et preesentia ostendit et preeterita enarrat, judicat quidem omnes, ipse autem a nemine judicatur. Nam judicat gentes, creature magis quam Oreatori servientes, et reprobabili mente universam suam operationem in vanum consumentes. Judicat autem etiam Judos, non percipientes verbum libertatis, neque volentes abire liberos, cum habeant preesentem liberatorem ; sed intempestive extra legem servire simulantes nihil indigenti Deo, et Christi adventum, quem propter salutem hominum fecit, non cognoseentes, neque intelligere volentes, quoniam duos adventus ejus omnes annuntiaverunt prophetee: unum quidem, in homo in plaga factus est, sciens ferre imbecillitatem, et in pullo asinee sedens, et reprobatus lapis ab eedificantibus, et sicut ovis ad victimam adductus, et per extensionem manuum dissolvens quidem Amalech; congregans autem dispersos filios a terminis terre in ovile Patris, et recommemoratus mortuorum suorum qui dormierant, et descendens ad eos, uti erueret eos®; secundum autem, in quo super nubes veniet, superducens diem que est sicut clibanus ardens, et percutiens terram verbo oris sui, et spiritu per labia sua interficiens impios, et ventilabrum in manu habens, et’ emundans aream suam, et triticum quidem in horreum comburens autem paleas igne inexstinguibili.
pass_a_gloss: The spiritual disciple indeed truly receiving the Spirit of God, who from the beginning in all dispositions of God was present to men, and announced future things and showed present things and narrated past things, judges indeed all, but he himself is judged by no one. For he judges the nations, creatures serving the Creator more, and with a reprobate mind consuming their whole operation in vain. And he judges also the Jews, not perceiving the word of liberty, nor willing to depart free, when they have a present liberator; but simulating to serve outside the law at an unseasonable time, needing nothing to God, and not knowing the advent of Christ, which he made for the salvation of men, nor willing to understand, since all the prophets announced two advents of him: one indeed, in which he was made in a plague of man, knowing to bear infirmity, and sitting on a foal of an ass, and a stone rejected by the builders, and as a sheep led to victim, and by the extension of hands dissolving Amalech; gathering however the dispersed sons from the ends of the earth into the fold of the Father, and being reminded of his own dead who slept, and descending to them, so that he might raise them; but the second, in which he will come upon the clouds, bringing a day which is like a burning furnace, and striking the earth with the word of his mouth, and killing the impious with the spirit through his lips, and having a winnowing fan in his hand, and purifying his floor, and gathering wheat indeed into a barn, but burning chaff with inextinguishable fire.
pass_b_english: The true spiritual disciple receives the Spirit of God, who has been present to humanity from the beginning, guiding God's plans and revealing what is to come, what is happening now, and what has happened in the past. This disciple has the authority to judge everyone, yet remains unjudged by anyone. The nations that prioritize created things over their Creator are subject to this judgment, as are those who waste their lives on meaningless pursuits. The Jews, too, are judged for failing to recognize the message of freedom and refusing to be liberated, despite having a Savior present with them. They go through the motions of serving God, but do so at the wrong time and without any real need for Him, unaware of Christ's first coming, which was for the salvation of humanity, and unwilling to understand that the prophets foretold not one, but two advents of Christ. In the first advent, Christ was born as a human, took on weakness, rode into Jerusalem on a donkey, was rejected by the builders, and was led to slaughter like a sheep, ultimately defeating Amalech through the power of His outstretched arms. Through this first coming, Christ gathered His scattered children from the ends of the earth into the Father's fold, remembered those who had died, and descended to them to raise them from the dead. In contrast, the second advent will be a time of reckoning, when Christ returns on the clouds, bringing a day of fiery judgment, striking the earth with the power of His word, and destroying the wicked with the breath of His mouth, all while separating the wheat from the chaff, gathering the wheat into His barn, and burning the chaff with an unquenchable fire.

review.notes: Pass B introduces significant interpretive additions and shifts in agency/modality not present in the Latin source. 1. The Latin 'in universis dispositionibus Dei' (in all the dispositions of God) is rendered in Pass B as 'guiding God's plans', which changes the theological meaning from the Spirit being present within God's arrangements to the Spirit actively directing them. 2. The Latin 'creature magis quam Oreatori servientes' (creatures serving the Creator more) is rendered in Pass B as 'The nations that prioritize created things over their Creator', which is an interpretive paraphrase rather than a translation. 3. The Latin 'per extensionem manuum dissolvens quidem Amalech' (by the extension of hands dissolving indeed Amalech) is rendered in Pass B as 'ultimately defeating Amalech through the power of His outstretched arms', which adds 'power' and 'ultimately' (interpretive expansion). 4. The Latin 'spiritu per labia sua interficiens impios' (killing the impious with the spirit through his lips) is rendered in Pass B as 'destroying the wicked with the breath of His mouth', which replaces 'spirit' with 'breath' and 'killing' with 'destroying'.
reasons: Pass B adds interpretive meaning to 'dispositionibus Dei' (guiding God's plans) and 'creature magis quam Oreatori servientes' (prioritize created things over their Creator) that is not in the Latin text.
Pass B adds 'power' to the description of the extension of hands: 'through the power of His outstretched arms' vs 'per extensionem manuum'.
Pass A gloss omits 'dissolvens quidem Amalech' from the source text.
Pass B English contains 'dissolving Amalech' but the source says 'dissolvens quidem Amalech', which is not fully captured in the translation.
Scripture check failed: the source contains 'dissolvens quidem Amalech' but no corresponding citation is provided in the English translation.
